subject: Scope update: add EU & APAC reserved pools for renewal
messages:
From: Sara Bloom <sara.bloom@atlashealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Renewal discussion — adding EU & APAC reserved pools

Hi Jordan,

We’re coming up on the end of our current Dedicated commitment (June 30). Procurement asked me to get ahead of the renewal conversation because our product team expects 2x traffic this fall due to a new patient-facing feature.

Immediate ask: can Redwood add dedicated pools in EU and APAC under the same commitment? High level requirements:
- ~80 additional vGPUs (equivalent to ~20 reserved nodes) split across eu-west and apac-southeast.
- Throughput target: sustain 18k token/s total at p95 across regions, with <120ms extra regional overhead for routing.
- Failover: warm standby between regions; we expect a documented failover runbook and failback timelines.

We’ll be evaluating pricing and term flexibility. Procurement prefers a 24-month term if we can lock pricing and get throughput guarantees / SLA language for cross-region failover.

Can you confirm feasibility and an initial estimate by end of week? Also include any operational notes (warm-up time, cache behavior) that will affect latency.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Bloom
Head of Platform Operations — Atlas Health
procurement@atlashealth.com

- Feasibility: yes — we can provision regional reserved pools and a warm standby failover path.
- Next steps I propose: 1) brief intake call with your infra + product to confirm traffic shape, 2) draft amendment with capacity and SLA language, 3) technical alignment with Redwood infra for warm standby timings.

For an initial sizing I’m attaching an estimate spreadsheet (attachment: initial-estimate.xlsx) that maps your 80 vGPU ask to node counts and expected token-throughput. At a high level: 20 reserved nodes (8 EU / 12 APAC) is a defensible starting point; we’ll propose a cross-region burst pool that can be used for short failovers.

A couple of questions to help refine estimates:
- Typical sequence lengths & p95 tokens per request? (affects KV-cache hit/miss and throughput)
- Expected synchronous vs. async request mix (sync chat vs background embedding jobs)
- Any regulatory constraints for data residency or audit retention beyond standard controls?

Marissa — looping you on pricing and SLA language. Neha/Connor — I’ll follow up with a separate thread for engineering runbook and latency expectations.

Best,

Jordan / team —

Quick operational response (ops-ready language you can forward):

1) Throughput & latency
- Based on the model profiles Atlas is running, a single reserved node (A100-equivalent, 80GB profile) sustains ~900–1,200 tokens/s at p95 for typical conversation loads. To reach ~18k token/s p95 across both regions we recommend reserving ~16–20 nodes in aggregate.
- Cross-region routing overhead: router-level add is typically 50–120ms depending on region egress and TLS handshake behavior. If Atlas pins users to nearest region and uses regional DNS-based routing, the additional overhead is closer to +50–70ms.

2) Warm standby and cache warm-up
- Cold-cache failovers can add up to 500ms per request for the initial burst as KV caches miss and kernels prime. To mitigate: maintain a small pre-warmed pool (2–3 nodes per region) for steady-state low-cost readiness, and use a short automated warm-up ramp (traffic replay for representative prompt sets) when failover is triggered.
- We can expose a pre-warm API to Atlas to trigger KV prefetch and generate synthetic heat for critical models. Expect pre-warm completion within 2–6 minutes depending on sequence lengths.

3) Recommended topology
- EU pool: 7 reserved nodes (primary), APAC pool: 9 reserved nodes (primary), Cross-region burst pool: 4 nodes (shared). Keep 2–3 nodes per region as pre-warm standby (count included above).
- Failover behavior: automatic routing to burst pool + pre-warmed nodes, telemetry-driven scaling within 2 minutes for expected <5 minute failovers.

4) SLA & guarantees (draftable items)
- Reserved capacity commitment: uptime on reserved nodes 99.9% monthly, with credits for sustained regional capacity loss >10 minutes.
- Throughput guarantee: committed baseline of 18k token/s p95 across regions; we’ll define measurement windows and telemetry endpoints.

Caveats / constraints
- If Atlas uses very long sequences (median > 1,500 tokens) throughput per node will drop ~20–30% — call this out in the amendment.
- Cold start impact depends heavily on cache priming and model size; quantized models warm faster.

I’ll draft a concise ops paragraph for the customer. Connor — can you confirm the burst pool orchestration steps and expected billing for cross-region bursts? Marissa — please confirm how this maps to our standard Dedicated amendment pricing tiers or if we need a custom proposal.

— Neha
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — adding EU & APAC reserved pools

Hi Sara — thanks for patience while we validated internally. Attached are the draft commercial and ops items we discussed. Summary below: 

Proposal summary (high level)
- Term: 24 months (preferred pricing lock) starting on the effective date of the amendment.
- Capacity: EU primary pool 7 reserved nodes; APAC primary pool 9 reserved nodes; Cross-region burst pool 4 nodes (hot standby). Total uplift: 20 reserved nodes (~80 vGPUs).
- Throughput & SLA: Committed baseline 18k token/s (p95) measured across configured telemetry endpoints. Reserved node uptime SLA: 99.9% per region. Credits apply for sustained capacity loss >10 minutes.
- Failover: Warm standby model — 2–3 pre-warmed nodes per region (included in counts). Expected pre-warm completion 2–6 minutes; automatic burst routing + telemetry-driven scaling for <5 minute failovers.

Commercials & next steps
- Price uplift: see attached addendum (redwood-eu-apac-addendum.pdf) for per-node monthly committed pricing and the cross-region burst charge schedule. We’re proposing a 6% discount on top of standard Dedicated pricing for the 24-month commit.
- Attachments: redwood-eu-apac-addendum.pdf; SLA-appendix.pdf; initial-estimate.xlsx (sent earlier).
- Legal: we’ll include a short SLA appendix that defines measurement windows, telemetry endpoints, and credit triggers.

If this looks good I can circulate a DocuSign amendment (I’ve prepped the HubSpot deal HB-2027-1147). Proposed timeline: sign within two weeks to secure capacity for Q3.

Requested action
- Sara / Procurement: confirm you’re comfortable with the node split and the proposed 24-month term + 6% discount.
- Atlas infra: if you can share a small sample of token-length distribution and peak-hour RPS by Tue morning we’ll lock final numbers.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-eu-apac-addendum.pdf (PDF, 6 pages); SLA-appendix.pdf (PDF, 3 pages); initial-estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet)
